question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\pi}{9}}^{- \frac{\pi}{18}} 6\cos\left(6 x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=6 x + \frac{\pi}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=6,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\pi}{9}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=6\left(- \frac{\pi}{9}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=- \frac{\pi}{6}\\ x=- \frac{\pi}{18}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=6\left(- \frac{\pi}{18}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{- \frac{\pi}{9}}^{- \frac{\pi}{18}} 6\cos\left(6 x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=6\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)\int_{- \frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\int_{- \frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=1\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{- \frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\\ &=1\left(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\sin\left(- \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=1\left(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{3}{2}} 5\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{\pi x}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\pi}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{\pi}{3}\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)=0\\ x=\frac{3}{2}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{\pi}{3}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{0}^{\frac{3}{2}} 5\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=5\left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right)\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{15}{\pi}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{15}{\pi}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\\ &=\frac{15}{\pi}\left(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\sin\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{15}{\pi}\left(\left(1\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{15}{\pi}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{3}{4}}^{\frac{3}{2}} 8\sin\left(\frac{2 \pi x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{2 \pi x}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{2 \pi}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{3}{2 \pi}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{3}{4}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{2 \pi}{3}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}\\ x=\frac{3}{2}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{2 \pi}{3}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)+\left(0\right)=\pi.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{\frac{3}{4}}^{\frac{3}{2}} 8\sin\left(\frac{2 \pi x}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=8\left(\frac{3}{2 \pi}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{12}{\pi}\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{12}{\pi}\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\\ &=- \frac{12}{\pi}\left(\cos\left(\pi\right)-\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{12}{\pi}\left(\left(-1\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{12}{\pi}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\pi}{10}}^{\frac{\pi}{30}} 4\sin\left(5 x + \frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=5 x + \frac{2 \pi}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=5,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\pi}{10}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=5\left(- \frac{\pi}{10}\right)+\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}\\ x=\frac{\pi}{30}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=5\left(\frac{\pi}{30}\right)+\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)=\frac{5 \pi}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{- \frac{\pi}{10}}^{\frac{\pi}{30}} 4\sin\left(5 x + \frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=4\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{4}{5}\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{4}{5}\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{5 \pi}{6}}\\ &=- \frac{4}{5}\left(\cos\left(\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right)-\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{4}{5}\left(\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{4 \sqrt{3}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{- \frac{\pi}{15}}^{\frac{\pi}{15}} \cos\left(- \frac{5 x}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=- \frac{5 x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=- \frac{5}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(- \frac{2}{5}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=- \frac{\pi}{15}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=- \frac{5}{2}\left(- \frac{\pi}{15}\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}\\ x=\frac{\pi}{15}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=- \frac{5}{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{15}\right)+\left(0\right)=- \frac{\pi}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

The transformed bounds decrease because the inner derivative is negative. Keep their order together with the negative substitution factor.

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{- \frac{\pi}{15}}^{\frac{\pi}{15}} \cos\left(- \frac{5 x}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x&=1\left(- \frac{2}{5}\right)\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{- \frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{2}{5}\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{- \frac{\pi}{6}} \cos\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=- \frac{2}{5}\left[\sin\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{- \frac{\pi}{6}}\\ &=- \frac{2}{5}\left(\sin\left(- \frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{2}{5}\left(\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
